answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one antique clock kept as a museum relic, restored and regulated by its holder at dawn every day under a licensed horologist's log. Random checks summon the holder to tune that exact clock live within hours, and one person cannot wind two clocks in two cities at the same dawn. The restoration fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real clock, another dawn shift, another human, and twice the prior fee, driving a farm's budget toward its nadir.
